evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK Chinese Character Database)
evidence.field: 形義通解; 小篆/金文; 說文; 廣韻; usage examples
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 紹 as 糸 semantic + 召 phonetic. It reports bronze forms with 幺 or 糸 and 召, sometimes with 卩; those inscriptions are used as surnames or personal names. Its quoted Shuowen entry says 繼也 (continue/inherit), adds 緊糾也 as an alternate gloss, and records 綤 as an old form written with 邵. The entry cites 尚書·盤庚上 紹復先王之大業 and 漢書·敘傳下 漢紹堯運 for the inheritance sense, and says the word later also means introduce. It records Guangyun 市沼切 and the Middle Chinese category 常開三宵上.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 - 字頭「紹」

evidence.text: The transmitted passage reads 紹復先王之大業, an attestation in the sense of resuming or carrying on the former kings’ enterprise. The web page presents a received text and does not establish the date of the wording’s composition or the earliest attestation.
evidence.title: Shang Shu: 盤庚

evidence.source: 漢字ペディア (Japan Kanji Aptitude Testing Foundation)
evidence.field: なりたち; meanings and readings
evidence.text: The entry describes 紹 as a phono-semantic formation of 糸 and phonetic 召 (セウ), with an explanation that joining threads extends to ‘succeed/inherit’; it also lists ‘mediate/introduce’ and ‘help’ among extended meanings. Modern Japanese readings listed are on ショウ and kun つぐ.
evidence.title: 紹 | 漢字一字

evidence.text: Unicode describes Unihan as a database of fields for Han ideographs and identifies fields by k-prefixed names. This official documentation establishes the database context, but does not verify the character-specific readings requested here.
evidence.title: UAX #38: Unicode Han Database (Unihan)

evidence.field: kMandarin rows for U+7D39 紹 and U+7ECD 绍
evidence.text: The supplied local rows give kMandarin shào for both 紹 and 绍. These rows are local dataset evidence only; the official character-specific GetUnihanData pages could not be opened in this web session, so no external character-page verification is claimed.

gaps: No visually inspected glyph images are reported. The CUHK entry lists small-seal and bronze forms, but this research did not independently inspect the glyph images or establish a detailed graphic-change sequence.

The earliest attestation date for 紹 and the chronology of its senses are not established here. Bronze use as names and received classical-text examples support distinct uses, but do not by themselves prove the semantic transition or its chronology.
The alternate Shuowen gloss 緊糾也 is recorded but its relation to the inheritance sense is not established.
CUHK reports no oracle-bone form in the entry display; this is not proof that no oracle-bone attestation exists.

Modern Mandarin comparison is available from the supplied local kMandarin rows (绍 and 紹 both shào), but official character-specific Unicode pages were inaccessible, so external click-through verification of those exact rows is missing.
No Baxter–Sagart local rows or checked source readings were provided in the input; no Old Chinese reconstruction comparison is asserted.
